# Competitor Intel Brief — 2026-10-27

# Section 1 — Executive Summary

The competitive field splits cleanly into three local Virginia players (Mermaid, Hampton Roads) and a national franchise (EcoWater), with no competitor publishing hard pricing—they all lead with "free water test" as the funnel entry point. Mermaid is the strongest direct NoVA threat this week: it's bundling plumbing + water treatment under one roof and running four stacked promotional offers ($200 heater, $100 new-customer, free install, free flush), which is an aggressive discount posture ClearWave should note. Hampton Roads is competing on warranty ("industry's most comprehensive Lifetime Warranty") and a trust/health angle rather than price. No competitor showed a material week-over-week change—all three prior snapshots are effectively identical to this week's, so there are no confirmed shifts yet, only a baseline to watch.

# Section 2 — Per-competitor table

| Competitor | Hero positioning (one phrase) | Distinct services | Pricing visible? | Notable shift this week |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mermaid Water | "Water treatment + plumbing from a local team that tests, installs, and stands behind the work" | Plumbing (water heaters, drain cleaning, fixtures), pump/pressure systems, Kinetico whole-home, commercial DI/RO | No hard prices, but 4 active promos ($200 off heater, $100 off first service, free Kinetico install, free heater flush) | No change vs. prior snapshot (title/meta identical); baseline established |
| EcoWater | "Better water starts here — global leader, free water test" | Softeners, filtration, smart-home leak/conservation tech, commercial, third-party certified systems | No — "consult a Water Pro" | No change vs. prior snapshot |
| Hampton Roads Water Services | "Full-service water quality experts — peace of mind, free test" | Water testing, hard-water/bacteria/contaminant treatment, air treatment, annual water-test program | No — "ask your representative" | No change vs. prior snapshot |

*(Brief covers the 3 competitors with full snapshots; 5 additional competitors referenced in context were not included in this week's data.)*

# Section 3 — Implications for ClearWave

- **Counter Mermaid's promo stack:** They're using four simultaneous discounts to win on perceived value. Test a single, clean "bundle" offer (e.g., free install or free first-year maintenance) rather than matching discount-for-discount, so ClearWave competes on value without a margin race.
- **Borrow the "free water test → diagnosis" funnel:** All three lead with it. If ClearWave isn't making a free in-home test the primary CTA above the fold, add it—it's the category-standard entry point.
- **Counter on warranty/recurring revenue:** Hampton Roads leads with "Lifetime Warranty"; Mermaid pushes annual/seasonal maintenance. Test a named warranty guarantee plus an annual-test subscription to lock in retention and a recurring-revenue hook neither owns outright.

# Section 4 — Watch items

- **Mermaid:** Watch whether the 4-offer promo stack rotates, expires, or adds pricing numbers—heavy promo activity may signal a demand push worth tracking.
- **Mermaid:** Monitor the Kinetico dealer positioning and any new service line (commercial RO/DI expansion).
- **All three:** No competitor shows list pricing—watch for anyone breaking ranks and publishing prices, which would reset the category.
- **EcoWater:** Watch the smart-home/leak-detection line; if a local dealer promotes it in NoVA, that's a new feature front ClearWave may need to answer.
- **Coverage gap:** Request snapshots for the 5 missing competitors next week to complete the landscape.

items.title: Water Minute · Why "free water tests" aren't really free
items.preview:
Words I like;
If the test is free, the test isn't the product. You are.
Here's something most folks don't know about the "free in-home water test" guys who knock on doors.
A lot of those tests are theater. The classic one is the soap trick. They put a little of your water in a vial, add a few drops of soap, shake it up, and when it doesn't lather they point and say, "See? Hard water, scum everywhere." Truth is, almost no water lathers well in that test. It's designed to fail. Then they add their treated water, it foams up nice, and suddenly you're signing paperwork at your kitchen table at 9pm.
A real test measures actual numbers. Hardness in grains, iron, pH, nitrates, bacteria if you're on a well. Numbers you can write down and verify. Not a magic trick meant to scare you.
If you already own one of our systems, this is exactly why you did your homework instead of buying off a pressure pitch. You bought on facts. That still holds up.
So before anyone shakes a vial at you, know what good water data actually looks like.
On a well and want the real numbers? Reply and I'll send you our free water assessment.
As promised, value in under a minute.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
